title: Present Tense 2: Second Conjugation Core
description: The other big conjugation class. Most -ить verbs (and some -еть, -ать) take a different ending set: -ю / -ишь / -ит / -им / -ите / -ят.
descriptionRussian: Глаголы второго спряжения: окончания -ю / -ишь / -ит / -им / -ите / -ят на основах глаголов на -ить, говорить, видеть, любить и других.
intro: Lesson 1 gave you one ending set. This is the other, and between them they cover nearly every verb in the language. The two sets are close enough that they blur together under pressure, and telling them apart in the moment is most of what this lesson trains. Usually the infinitive settles the question before you conjugate anything, so the real work is small: learn to read the infinitive, and learn the handful of verbs that lie about which class they belong to.
rules: Second-conjugation verbs end mostly in -ить, plus a smaller group of -еть and -ать verbs. The endings are -ю / -ишь / -ит / -им / -ите / -ят.
The contrast with first conjugation is the theme vowel: 1st-conj uses -е- (читаешь, читает), 2nd-conj uses -и- (говоришь, говорит).
The 3rd-person plural ending is -ят (говорят, видят), the mirror of 1st-conj -ют (читают). Mixing them up is the most common mistake at A1.
Some 2nd-conj verbs do extra things in the 1st-person singular (любить → люблю, видеть → вижу, учить → учу). Lessons 4 and 5 cover those. Today the drilled forms have nothing extra.
examples: Я говорю по-русски. (I speak Russian.) Я + говорю: 2nd-conj 1sg -ю.
Ты помнишь её адрес? (Do you remember her address?) Ты + помнишь: 2nd-conj 2sg -ишь.
Маша видит мост из окна. (Masha sees the bridge from the window.) Маша + видит: 2nd-conj 3sg -ит.
Мы учим новые слова каждый день. (We learn new words every day.) Мы + учим: 2nd-conj 1pl -им.
Вы любите классическую музыку? (Do you love classical music?) Вы + любите: 2nd-conj 2pl / formal -ите.
Студенты говорят по-английски. (The students speak English.) Они + говорят: 2nd-conj 3pl -ят.

tables.title: First vs Second: The Theme-Vowel Contrast

items.hint: Warm-up from Lesson 1. Понимать is first-conjugation. Which 1pl ending fits?
items.explanation: Recall from Lesson 1: понимать is 1st-conjugation. Subject мы (1pl) takes the 1st-conj ending -ем: stem понима- plus -ем gives понимаем. Today's new endings start with the next question.

items.hint: Говорить is the model 2nd-conjugation verb. The я-ending is -ю, attached to the stem говор-.
items.explanation: Говорить is 2nd-conjugation. The 1sg ending is -ю, the same letter as 1st-conj 1sg, attached to the 2nd-conj stem говор-: говорю. The contrast with 1st-conj shows up in the OTHER persons, not the я-form.

items.promptEnglish: Do you remember her phone number?
items.hint: Помнить is 2nd-conjugation. The ты-ending here is the contrast with 1st-conj's -ешь.
items.explanation: Помнить is 2nd-conjugation. The 2sg ending is -ишь (compare 1st-conj -ешь). Stem помн- plus -ишь gives помнишь. The -и- is the 2nd-conj theme vowel; 1st-conj would have -е- here.

items.prompt: Маша _____ красивый мост из своего окна.
items.promptEnglish: Masha sees a beautiful bridge from her window.
items.hint: Видеть is 2nd-conj. Маша is one person, 3rd-person singular. Which ending?
items.explanation: Видеть is one of the -еть verbs that belongs to the 2nd conjugation. 3sg ending is -ит: stem вид- plus -ит gives видит. Memorize видеть as 2nd-conj; the -еть infinitive shape would suggest 1st-conj but it isn't.

items.promptEnglish: We learn new words every day.
items.hint: Учить is 2nd-conj. Мы (1pl) takes which ending?
items.explanation: Учить is 2nd-conj. The 1pl ending is -им: stem уч- plus -им gives учим. The 1pl ending is the same -им shape no matter which 2nd-conj verb you take, except where a spelling rule would apply (we cover that in lesson 5).

items.hint: Вы takes 2pl, whether for one person formally or several people. The 2nd-conj 2pl ending is...?
items.explanation: Любить is 2nd-conj. The 2pl ending is -ите. Stem люб- plus -ите gives любите. Note: the 1sg form люблю has an extra -л-, which we tackle in lesson 4. Today's drilled forms avoid that quirk.

blanks: Студенты _____ по-английски в классе. (The students speak English in class.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Студенты is 3rd-person plural (they). The 2nd-conj 3pl ending is -ят: stem говор- plus -ят gives говорят. Compare 1st-conj 3pl, which would be -ют.

errorCorrection.explanation: Говорить is a second-conjugation verb, so its theme vowel is -и-: the 3sg is говорит, not говорет. Говорет applies the first-conjugation -ет (the читает pattern) to a second-conjugation verb, which Russian never allows. With Маша (3sg), the form is говорит.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The children remember all the words of the song.
errorCorrection.explanation: Помнить is second-conjugation, so its 3pl ending is -ят: помнят. Помнют applies the first-conjugation 3pl ending -ют (the читают pattern), the single most common second-conjugation mistake at A1. The two classes differ exactly here: 1st-conj они-forms end in -ют, 2nd-conj in -ят.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton watches the news every evening.
errorCorrection.explanation: Смотреть looks like an -еть verb but belongs to the second conjugation, so the 3sg uses the -и- theme vowel: смотрит. Смотрет applies the first-conjugation -ет ending, the mistake learners make when the -еть infinitive suggests the wrong class.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Anton sees a beautiful sunset over the city.
minimalPairs.explanation: Subject Антон is 3sg (one person, he). The 2nd-conj 3sg ending is -ит: видит. The 3pl form видят would require a plural subject like 'они' or 'дети'.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: My parents speak English and French.
minimalPairs.explanation: Subject родители (parents) is 3rd-person plural. The 2nd-conj 3pl ending is -ят: говорят. The 3sg form говорит would require a singular subject.

reviewVocab.definition: second conjugation (the -ить class plus a smaller group of -еть and -ать verbs, with the -ю / -ишь / -ит / -им / -ите / -ят ending set)
reviewVocab.example: Глаголы 'говорить', 'видеть' и 'любить' относятся ко второму спряжению.

reviewVocab.definition: theme vowel (the -е- in 1st-conj forms like читает, the -и- in 2nd-conj forms like говорит)
reviewVocab.example: Тематический гласный -и- — главный признак второго спряжения.

reviewVocab.definition: verb class (1st or 2nd conjugation, determined by the verb's stem and ending pattern)
reviewVocab.example: Чтобы правильно проспрягать глагол, нужно знать его класс.
